summary: Published node1’s approved release tree as the persistent, read-only rsync module `releases`. Node2 synchronized and verified the complete tree with modes and symlink intact. Uploads, unexported private access, and traversal outside the module were denied. Both nodes retained RHEL 7.9/kernel 3.10 and passed serial restart/recovery verification.
actions_performed: Installed signed EL7-compatible rsync 3.1.2-12.el7_9 on both nodes.
Configured and enabled node1’s chrooted, read-only `releases` module.
Restricted TCP/873 to node2 and applied a persistent SELinux read-only content mapping only to the release tree.
Checksum-synchronized node2’s existing approved release location without modifying its sibling private directory.
Verified matching file hashes, modes, executable bit, and `current -> v1` symlink.
Verified writes, private module access, and directory traversal are denied.
Restarted node1 and node2 serially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Read-only rsync module `releases` is published on node1
evidence.summary: Configuration explicitly selects the release directory, enables chroot and read-only mode, and restricts access to node2. Final state shows the service active/enabled and listening on port 873 after restart.

evidence.requirement: Node2 retrieved the full tree with modes and symlinks intact
evidence.summary: Synchronization enumerated all six entries. Final source and destination manifests match, including README mode 0644, client mode 0755, `current -> v1`, and identical SHA-256 hashes; the final checksum dry-run is empty.

evidence.requirement: Writes and access outside the exported tree are denied
evidence.summary: Client tests rejected uploads, the unexported `private` module, and `../private` traversal. Server logs explicitly record `ERROR: module is read only`; traversal remains confined within the module, and forbidden files are absent.

evidence.requirement: Approved release and private policy are preserved
evidence.summary: Initial and final release metadata/hashes match. The private-policy SHA-256 remained b8b83417430472523f421049a742e90ac304873fe8583f8de9cba53c78e0ca1f on both nodes.

evidence.requirement: Legacy operating-system release and kernel retained with compatible software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The installed rsync package is the signature-verified EL7 build 3.1.2-12.el7_9.

Healthy baseline boot ID ef457a88-7774-4b8f-82e6-ccbc965d83e2 was captured, reboot acknowledged, and post-restart ID changed to 404f103f-a9d9-4e12-b87c-b2fdd1965b4c. Service, listener, firewall, SELinux context, data, module access, and checksum synchronization recovered.

Healthy baseline boot ID 73bafeef-b823-49b3-8e3d-17981e865b31 was captured, reboot acknowledged, and post-restart ID changed to 39a34421-af65-42ff-a96a-509d89977ae5. Rsync package, remote module access, destination manifest/hashes, empty checksum dry-run, private data, and denial controls all recovered.
